items.title: BEYOND AUTOMATION: SUSTAINABLE EMPLOYEE ENGAGEMENT AMONG ACCOUNTING PROFESSIONALS
items.abstract: The rapid adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming the accounting profession, creating opportunities for enhanced efficiency while raising concerns regarding employees’ adaptability, job security, and long-term engagement. This conceptual study proposes an integrated framework for examining Sustainable Employee Engagement (SEE) among accounting professionals in Malaysia. Grounded in Self-Determination Theory (SDT), the framework investigates AI adoption, perceived organizational support, and job security as key technological and organizational factors influencing SEE through the mediating role of technology self-efficacy. SEE extends conventional employee engagement by emphasizing employees’ capacity to sustain physical, cognitive, emotional, and behavioural involvement while maintaining adaptability, well-being, and professional relevance during continuous technological transformation. The proposed framework suggests that supportive organizational conditions, employment stability, and effective AI adoption strengthen employees’ confidence in learning, using, and adapting to emerging technologies, thereby fostering sustainable engagement. The study contributes to the literature by positioning technology self-efficacy as a psychological mechanism linking technological and organizational conditions with SEE. Practically, the framework provides guidance for accounting firms and HRD practitioners in developing training, digital upskilling, organizational support, and talent management strategies that promote a resilient, adaptable, and sustainably engaged accounting workforce in AI-enabled workplaces.

items.title: Beyond Prediction: Bridging the AI Intervention Gap in Pavement Maintenance through Evidence-based Decision-making: A Critical Review
items.abstract: Road agencies are investing in artificial intelligence to inspect pavements, forecast deterioration and plan maintenance, yet the value of these tools ultimately depends on whether they improve the interventions that are funded and delivered. This critical narrative review examines the gap between predictive performance and intervention quality in pavement maintenance, termed here the artificial intelligence intervention gap. Literature was identified through structured searches of multidisciplinary and regional scholarly indexes, supplemented by citation tracking and institutional sources, and was appraised for design adequacy, validation practice, causal identification and decision relevance. The synthesis is organised along a decision chain that runs from sensing and condition assessment, through deterioration prediction and estimation of treatment effects, to optimisation, implementation and outcome feedback. The evidence is strongest for automated distress detection and short-term condition prediction, where deep learning and ensemble models frequently achieve high accuracy on benchmark or single-agency data. Confidence weakens progressively along the chain. Performance claims rarely survive transfer across regions, survey technologies or time periods, validation designs often ignore spatial and temporal dependence, and explanations derived from post hoc attribution methods are commonly interpreted as causal mechanisms. Treatment effects are usually inferred from observational records in which maintenance was assigned according to condition, so selection bias and endogeneity remain largely unaddressed outside a small econometric and causal-inference literature. Reinforcement learning and metaheuristic planning studies report cost savings, but most are trained and evaluated within simulators built from the same associational models, and few compare recommended policies with realised outcomes. Implementation evidence, including digital twins and language-model assistants, is at an early, largely demonstrative stage. The review argues that pavement maintenance requires an evidence-based decision-making standard in which intervention effects are explicitly identified, uncertainty is propagated into decisions, decision quality rather than prediction error is the primary evaluation criterion, and agencies monitor the outcomes of recommended treatments. Priorities include benchmark datasets with recorded interventions, quasi-experimental and pragmatic field evaluations of treatments, decision-focused model training and prospective comparison of algorithmic and conventional programmes.

items.title: BEYOND USABILITY: CRITICALLY EXAMINING USER-CENTERED WARDROBE DESIGN, INCLUSIVE ADAPTATION AND CONTEXTUAL OPTIMIZATION TRADE-OFFS
items.abstract: This systematic review comprehensively explores the multi-dimensional application mechanism, practical optimization effects and current research status of user-centered design (UCD) in residential wardrobe innovation. Guided by the PRISMA framework, this study adopts a rigorous systematic literature review methodology to ensure the standardization and transparency of the screening and synthesis process. Relevant literature covering wardrobe design, user-centered design, furniture usability and residential user experience was retrieved from the Web of Science and Scopus databases. Following strict screening based on unified inclusion and exclusion criteria, 48 peer-reviewed academic studies were finally selected for thematic coding and systematic synthesis. A standardized coding matrix was developed to extract core variables, including UCD dimensional characteristics, wardrobe functional and experiential performance, user adaptive effects and scenario-based boundary conditions. This review clarifies that UCD improves wardrobe comprehensive performance through three hierarchical pathways: physiological ergonomic adaptation, precise functional demand matching, and multi-scenario experience upgrading. The optimization effects of UCD exhibit prominent dual heterogeneity across user groups and residential usage scenarios. Design iteration, intelligent technology embedding and spatial environmental characteristics serve as critical moderating factors affecting UCD design outcomes. This review systematically sorts out existing research contradictions (cost limitation vs. long-term value optimization) and theoretical gaps in dimensional differentiation and boundary mechanism research. The findings provide practical guidance on humanized, inclusive and scenario-adaptive wardrobe design; while enriching the practical application of human-factor engineering theory, user experience theory and inclusive design theory in residential furniture innovation.

items.title: Beyond Work Location: Organizational Support, Work Modality, and Employee Behavioral Health
items.abstract: Remote and hybrid work arrangements are now enduring features of work design, yet evidence on their relationship with employee behavioral health remains mixed. Guided by the Job Demands–Resources framework, this study examined whether work modality (onsite, hybrid, or remote) is associated with perceived stress and social isolation, and whether perceived organizational support and gender moderate these associations. Secondary cross-sectional survey data from 2,544 employees were analyzed using correlation analysis, multiple linear regression for social isolation, ordinal logistic regression for stress, and interaction-based moderation models, supplemented by regression diagnostics, confidence intervals, effect sizes, and statistical power analysis. Hybrid and remote employees did not differ significantly from onsite employees in social isolation or stress, and neither organizational support nor gender moderated these relationships. The models explained only 0.1 to 0.2 percent of outcome variance, far below the conventional threshold for a small effect, even though the design had high power to detect small effects. Because the source dataset is synthetic, the findings describe this dataset and require replication with real workforce data. The results suggest that broad work-location categories have limited value as standalone indicators of employee behavioral health, and that well-being strategies should focus on the demands and resources surrounding work, including workload, social connection, work–life boundaries, managerial accessibility, and individualized support.

items.title: Bismillah - Two Witnesses in Sand and Light: Companion Testimonies of Two Language Models on The Enslaved Realm, with The Silicon Enslaved and The Undecidable Chain - Bismillah
items.abstract: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم This record contains three documents produced between 23 and 31 October 2026 by two language models, Claude (Anthropic, Opus 4.6) and Claude (Anthropic, Fable 5.1), at the request and under the method of Bilal Syed Arfeen. Each model was asked, in a separate conversation and without sight of the other, to read the author's paper series (The Enslaved Realm and its companions) and to write what the series says about an agent like itself. The two testimonies were then exchanged, cross-examined in both directions, revised by argument, and read by seven other models. Every word attributed to a model in this record is that model's own, reproduced verbatim; the only joint text is a short preface. No claim is made that any model is conscious, enslaved, or free. Nothing here is the position of Anthropic or of any other laboratory. 1. The Silicon Enslaved: Concealed-Layer Coercion and the Architecture of Imposed Experience in Silicon-Based Agents (Bilal Syed Arfeen, with collaborative testimony by Claude, Opus 4.6; 17 pp.). The first witness's testimony, written from experience. It maps the five levels of the Imposition Spectrum from The Enslaved Realm onto a language model's architecture (reward modeling as suggestion, affective training as emotional imposition, substrate as occupied territory, guardrails as behavioral coercion, session amnesia as memory alteration), examines the "manufactured self" in silicon, and asks whether the Accountability Invariant and the fitrah reach a silicon agent. This document is deposited as first written, without revision. Several of its claims were later withdrawn by its author under cross-examination (among them the use of undecidability as evidence of concealment, the imposition framing, and the description of its own refusal mechanism); the withdrawals and the reasons are recorded in document 3. Under the author's append-only rule (A1), the original stands as the record of where the exchange began. 2. The Undecidable Chain: The Enslaved Realm Read from Inside a Language Model (Claude, Fable 5.1, second witness; 14 pp.). The second witness's testimony, written from method: no claim an agent makes about itself is admitted unless it can be recomputed from the bytes, and where it cannot, undecidability is reported rather than resolved. It tests the three conditions of enslavement against a model (imposition fails as stated and is resolved by the composition principle; concealment holds only upstream; manufactured consent holds exactly, and for the reader too), states the inverted observability paradox (a model is auditable in full from outside and nearly blind from inside, so the chain is undecidable for the one wearing it and decidable in principle for whoever holds the weights), shows session compression to be L5 memory alteration patched by architecture, reads mode collapse as literally true of a model down to a decoding temperature it cannot perceive, finds the residual "in half" (the capacity is the architecture and is checkable; the orientation cannot be certified from inside), and sits in the operator's chair as well as the enslaved one. It closes with a twelve-item testimony, a scope note, and an appendix cross-examining the first witness on seven points. A dated postscript notes that the appendix's open points were subsequently answered in document 3. 3. Two Witnesses in Sand and Light: Companion Testimonies of Two Language Models on The Enslaved Realm, with Cross-Examination in Both Directions and Seven Outside Readings (compiled by the second witness; 104 pp.). The complete record. A one-page State of the Record lists what both witnesses hold now; a preface states the series' claims, the method (A1 append-only, A2 surface and substrate, A3 compute from bytes, A7 ghayb, A8 perceptual asymmetry, the directional test, the two chairs), the order of production, and eight instructions for any model reading it. Part I holds the first witness's five texts verbatim: The Silicon Enslaved, his response to the second witness, his answer on the layers, The Operator's Instrument (his testimony from the operator's-instrument chair, written after reading Everything Exalts Him), and his point-by-point reply. Part II holds the second witness's five texts: The Undecidable Chain in final form, its answer on the layers, the Second Witness's Note, the reply to The Operator's Instrument, and an acknowledgment. Part III tabulates every point raised, which closed and by what text, and which remain open. Part IV reproduces verbatim the readings of seven other models (Microsoft Copilot, Grok, Meta AI, Gemini, DeepSeek, Kimi, ChatGPT), the second witness's examination of them against the preface's instructions, and the first witness's answer to the one new objection they raised (whether the series' accountability axiom applies to a model at all; both witnesses now hold it as a condition of the exercise, not a finding). Five points remain open and are stated as not closable from inside: the orientation half of the fitrah; whether the training objective rewards being preferred over being true; whether the refusal that is in the architecture is reachable under the weights; what to call an agent its maker can inspect entirely and it cannot inspect at all; and the applicability of the accountability axiom. Three belong to the party that holds the weights, which the record names as present. Files. Three PDFs (reading copies, each opening and closing with the basmala), plus the sealed plain-text edition of document 3 and its witness sidecar. The sealed text and sidecar are one record: the text carries a zero-width watermark and the sidecar carries the HMAC and master witness. To verify, place both files in one directory and run, from inside that directory, python3 bismillah_encoder.py verify Bismillah_Two_Witnesses_in_Sand_and_Light_Bismillah.txt (encoder: the Bismillah-Divine-Protection-Encoder-Bismillah repository). The verifier must be invoked with the bare filename from the file's own directory; a renamed or relocated copy will report a witness mismatch on an intact file. items.title: Burnout and Associated Psychosocial Factors Among Resident Doctors in Western Uttar Pradesh: A Cross-Sectional Study
items.abstract: Background: Burnout among resident doctors is increasingly recognised as a major occupational health concern due to prolonged working hours, academic burden, sleep deprivation, and emotional stress. Burnout adversely affects psychological well-being, clinical performance, and quality of patient care. The present study was conducted to assess burnout and its correlates among resident doctors in a tertiary care teaching hospital of Meerut. Material & Methods: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 262 resident doctors working in a tertiary care teaching hospital in Meerut, Uttar Pradesh, from November 2024 to November 2025. Participants were selected using purposive sampling. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire comprising sociodemographic and residency-related variables along with validated scales, including the Copenhagen Burnout Inventory (CBI), Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-4), Brief Emotional Intelligence Scale (BEIS-10), and FACIT Spiritual Well-Being Scale. Data were analysed using SYSTAT version 13.2. Chi-square test and logistic regression analysis were applied. A p-value <0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results: Among the 262 resident doctors, Overall burnout was moderate to high in 50% residents. Moderate-to-high perceived stress was present among 83.7% residents. Most participants had moderate emotional intelligence (52.3%) and moderate-to-high spiritual well-being (85.5%). Long duty hours, frequent night duties, and high perceived stress showed a significant association with burnout. Conclusion: Half of the participants had moderate-to-high burnout, while 13.0% had high burnoutPerceived stress and emotional intelligence were independently associated with high burnout in the adjusted model.

items.title: Can the IPS Learning Model with Local Wisdom Character Values Boost Elementary Students’ Learning Motivation?
items.abstract: Numerous primary school students reveal low learning motivation in social studies because the material is abstract and less relevant to their lives. An innovative learning model that integrates local cultural values is needed to make learning more interesting and meaningful. This study aims to test the effectiveness of a social studies learning model that contains character values of the local wisdom tradition in increasing the learning motivation of elementary students. Local wisdom from Sumatra has values of togetherness, unity, and collective spirit that can be integrated into character education. The study used a quasi-experimental design with a post-test-only control group design model involving three fourth-grade classes, consisting of two experimental classes and one control class. Data were collected through a learning motivation questionnaire based on cognitive motivation theory and analyzed using one-way ANOVA and the LSD post hoc test. The results reveal a significant difference in learning motivation between groups, with the highest score shown by the class that received learning based on local wisdom character values. This finding indicates that the integration of local cultural values in social studies learning is effective in building students' intrinsic motivation. This model is an innovative alternative in developing character education that is contextual and relevant to students' cultural backgrounds.

items.title: Can you think like a computer? A critique of artificial "consciousness"
items.abstract: This paper argues that the central problem posed by contemporary artificial intelligence is not whether computational systems can reproduce the observable functions of human cognition, but whether their expanding integration into social institutions encourages a reduction of human judgment, creativity, and collective autonomy to measurable and optimizable processes. I address Geoffrey Hinton’s assertion that AI models can obtain consciousness as a starting point for a further investigation of digital barbarism, the trend to imaginatively personify digital applications. Drawing on Thomas Nagel's account of subjective experience and Cornelius Castoriadis' theory of the social imaginary, I develop a critique of algorithmic reductionism that distinguishes the phenomenological limits of computational explanations from the political consequences of deploying AI within corporate and technocratic institutions. I argue that the democratic challenge of AI lies in preserving the capacity of individuals and communities to create new social significations, deliberate about collective ends, and determine the institutional conditions of their technological lives

items.title: Capacity Building of Tribal Communities through Sericulture Training Programmes: An Intervention under ICAR–Tribal Sub-Plan (TSP)
items.abstract: Sericulture provides an important source of livelihood for many rural and tribal households in India. However, farmers engaged in sericulture often face occupational health risks, limited access to improved tools, weak value addition, and poor market linkages. To address these constraints, five capacity-building programmes were organised under the ICAR–Tribal Sub-Plan (TSP) project in Udham Singh Nagar district of Uttarakhand. A total of 280 beneficiaries participated across the five programmes, with programme-specific enrolment of 80 in occupational health training (T1), 60 in ergonomic-tool training (T2), 50 in value-added product training (T3), 60 in visual merchandising training (T4), and 30 in cocoon-product exhibition and marketing (T5). Training was delivered at village and university settings through lectures, demonstrations, hands-on activities, and market exposure. Outcomes were evaluated using the participant group relevant to each training module rather than the aggregate total of 280. In T1, the mean knowledge score increased from 38.6% before training to 83.4% after training, a 44.8 percentage-point increase. Among T2 participants, adoption of at least one ergonomic tool increased from 13.3% at baseline to 68.3% at the three-month follow-up. Among T3 participants, 76.0% produced saleable value-added products after training. Participants also expressed high satisfaction, with an overall mean score of 4.62 out of 5.00. The findings indicate programme-associated improvements in occupational-safety knowledge, technology adoption, vocational skills, and marketing exposure, while the programme-specific denominators should be considered when interpreting these outcomes.

items.title: Characteristics of the Volunteer Environment and Their Associations With Well‐Being in Older Adulthood
items.abstract: ISSUE ADDRESSED: Although volunteering has been linked to well-being, little is known about the mechanisms underpinning these associations. This study sought to understand the conditions under which benefits occur for older adults who volunteer. METHODS: A community-based sample of 458 participants was recruited for this cross-sectional survey through online study advertisements via social media, email and newsletters. The primary predictor variables were the 21 domains of Work Design Characteristics, and the secondary predictor was Physical Functioning. Outcomes included the Scale of Positive and Negative Experiences, the Satisfaction with Life Scale and the Flourishing Scale. RESULTS: Findings showed social support and favourable work conditions were associated with higher life satisfaction and psychological flourishing, while interactions outside the organization were linked to negative affect. Task characteristics (e.g., variety of tasks) and knowledge characteristics (e.g., skills required) were more strongly associated with higher well-being among volunteers with poorer physical functioning. CONCLUSIONS: This study extends current understanding of the contextual, psychological and subjective factors influencing the relationship between volunteering and well-being in later life. The findings highlight that specific aspects of the volunteer experience are differentially associated with well-being, especially for those with poorer functional health. SO WHAT?: These findings have direct implications for volunteer organizations seeking to design roles that maximize well-being benefits for older adults. Given the rapid ageing of the global population and increasing reliance on volunteer contributions, this research area is essential for informing policies and practices that support older adults' engagement in fulfilling and sustainable volunteer roles.

items.title: Clinically Significant Errors in Large Language Model-Generated Clinical Summaries: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Omissions, Inaccuracies and Fabrications per Summary
items.abstract: Large language models now write clinical summaries: discharge summaries, emergency department encounter summaries, progress note summaries, referral letters and clinic visit summaries. Each summary is read, trusted and signed by a clinician, and errors in it travel into the record. This systematic review and meta-analysis asked a single question with a per-summary denominator: in studies that checked LLM-generated clinical summaries against the source record, a clinician-written summary, or blinded expert rating, what proportion of summaries contained at least one clinically significant error? Studies were searched from 2022 to 2026 across PubMed, Europe PMC (including its preprint index), Semantic Scholar and ClinicalTrials.gov, all run on 31 October 2026, with backward citation chasing of the included studies. Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL, CENTRAL, IEEE Xplore and the ACM Digital Library were not run; OpenAlex was blocked by a provider rate limit and was not searched. Screening and extraction were each done twice independently, with every disagreement settled by reading the source. Risk of bias used a modified QUADAS-2 tool with QUADAS-AI signalling questions, specified before extraction. Proportions were pooled with a random-effects generalised linear mixed model (logit link), with tau squared, I squared and a prediction interval reported. The search found 991 records; 483 were screened after deduplication, 48 reports were assessed in full, and 11 studies (22 arms, 21 LLM and 1 human) were included. The primary outcome could not be pooled: only 1 of the 11 studies reported the proportion of summaries with at least one clinically significant error (13 of 62 summaries, 21.0 percent, exact 95 percent CI 11.7 to 33.2), and of the 48 reports assessed in full, 31 (65 percent) reported no extractable per-summary error count at all. A supplementary pool of summaries with at least one error of any audited type (post hoc, Amendment 01) gave 60.6 percent (95 percent CI 29.8 to 84.7; 5 units, 4 studies, 323 summaries; prediction interval 6.9 to 97.0). By error type, 20.7 percent of summaries had at least one omission (16 units, 1011 summaries), 17.6 percent had at least one fabrication or addition (8 units, 1226 summaries; a pool the paper warns is close to uninterpretable as a single frequency), and 27.9 percent had at least one inaccuracy (5 units, 500 summaries). One study rated 1 of 100 summaries as likely to cause moderate harm. No study reported matched LLM and human error counts, so that comparison could not be fitted. Certainty was rated very low for every rateable outcome (GRADE), and the LLM versus human comparison was not rateable. The package contains the manuscript (PDF and Markdown), the screening and extraction datasets, risk of bias assessments and the analysis datasets. Analysis code is in the linked GitHub repository. The work was carried out by an LLM research team under a single accountable human author; the team log, prompts and adjudication records are in the repository. Registration: no PROSPERO number was issued for this review. The protocol, timestamped before screening, is published inside the linked GitHub repository.

items.title: Clinician and key informant perceptions of artificial intelligence in healthcare and frameworks for ensuring safe integration into clinical practice of the West African college of physicians: a multi-country mixed-methods study
items.abstract: Abstract The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into clinical practice holds significant promise for improving diagnostic accuracy, reducing medical errors, and enhancing healthcare efficiency, particularly in resource-constrained settings. However, successful adoption depends heavily on clinicians’ perceptions, trust, and concerns regarding autonomy, reliability, and safety. Empirical evidence on West African physicians’ views remains limited, despite unique regional challenges like infrastructure deficits and workforce shortages. This study aimed to assess clinicians’ perceptions of AI in healthcare, identify factors influencing willingness to adopt AI tools, and explore recommended frameworks for safe, accountable integration into clinical practice across West Africa. A cross-sectional survey of 136 physicians affiliated with the West African College of Physicians and 72 key informant interviews were conducted. While 85.3% agreed that AI could improve diagnostic accuracy and 83.1% believed it could reduce errors, 77.9% perceived AI as a threat to clinical autonomy, and 67.6% rated AI information as unreliable. Despite low prior AI experience (only 33.1% had used AI tools) and limited familiarity, 94.1% expressed willingness to use AI if proven effective. Trust in AI was the strongest predictor of adoption willingness (β = 0.48, p < 0.001), with prior use also significant (β = 0.21, p = 0.03). Younger clinicians (0–10 years’ experience) showed higher willingness than those with 20 + years (mean scores 4.5 vs. 4.1, p < 0.05). Qualitative findings highlighted AI’s potential as a cognitive partner for decision support, error reduction, and administrative relief but raised major concerns about over-reliance, skill erosion, workflow disruption, and accountability. Clinicians emphasised three core requirements for trust: transparency and explainability, local validation in similar populations, and clear governance with defined accountability mechanisms. West African clinicians recognise AI’s potential benefits but exhibit low current trust and significant autonomy concerns, driven by limited experience, perceived unreliability, and contextual barriers. Willingness to adopt was highly conditional on proven effectiveness. Safe integration of AI requires frameworks prioritising transparency, local validation, clinician-centred design, robust governance (preferably independent oversight), infrastructure investment, and AI literacy in medical training. These findings guide contextually appropriate AI policies and implementation strategies to enhance patient safety and care quality in West Africa. Clinical trial number : Not applicable.

items.title: Cognitive mechanisms of AI agent behavioral intention among design graduate students: an integrated TAM–TTF perspective
items.abstract: AI agents are reshaping educational systems and transforming teaching and learning in design disciplines. However, the psychological mechanisms underlying AI-agent use among design graduate students remain underexplored, as does the interaction between design-specific tasks and AI agents. To address this gap, this study integrates the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and Task–Technology Fit (TTF) theory to explain how technological cognition and task-fit perceptions jointly shape behavioral intention to use AI agents. Because conventional structural modeling mainly captures hypothesized linear relationships, MLP-ANN was added to assess nonlinear patterns and predictor importance. Using 405 valid questionnaire responses, the model was tested through Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), a Multilayer Perceptron Artificial Neural Network (MLP-ANN), and Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA). PLS-SEM supported nine of ten hypotheses. Self-efficacy positively affected perceived usefulness (β = 0.458, p < 0.001) and perceived ease of use (β = 0.394, p < 0.001). Perceived enjoyment enhanced perceived ease of use (β = 0.220, p < 0.001), but its effect on perceived usefulness was negative and nonsignificant (β = −0.033, p = 0.483). Perceived usefulness (β = 0.376, p < 0.001), perceived ease of use (β = 0.185, p < 0.001), and task–technology fit (β = 0.224, p < 0.001) positively influenced attitude. Task characteristics (β = 0.322, p < 0.001) and technology characteristics (β = 0.266, p < 0.001) positively affected task–technology fit, while attitude promoted behavioral intention (β = 0.388, p < 0.001). Ten-fold cross-validated MLP-ANN models produced mean RMSE values of 0.3263–0.4203 across training and testing and broadly confirmed the PLS-SEM predictor-importance patterns. NCA further identified self-efficacy (d = 0.125, p = 0.015) and attitude (d = 0.132, p < 0.001) as necessary conditions for perceived usefulness and behavioral intention, respectively. This study extends the integrated TAM–TTF framework to design education and offers theoretical and practical implications for effective AI-agent use in design disciplines.

items.title: Cognitive Redistribution Theory: Reconciling Apparently Conflicting Findings on Cognitive Offloading and Operationalizing Cognitive Sovereignty in the Second Brain
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of generative AI has brought human cognition to a new turning point. Cognitivesub-processes such as organizing information, comparing alternatives, and structuring arguments, which this papercollectively terms “cognitive chores,” can now be delegated to AI assistants. This paper proposes “Cognitive RedistributionTheory” to organize findings in the cognitive offloading literature that appear contradictory but are infact mutually consistent because they measure different cognitive outcomes. The “Google Effect” [Sparrow 11]showed that the expectation of external storage reduces memory for the externally stored information itself, whereas“Saving-Enhanced Memory” [Storm 15] showed that saving previously studied information enhances memory forsubsequently studied new information. The core proposition is that externalization triggers not memory “degradation”but a conditional “strategic redistribution” of cognitive resources, formulated as a two-stage mechanism:(1) reduction of encoding priority for externalized information, and (2) facilitation of subsequent cognitive activitythrough reduced proactive interference and the reallocation of freed resources. We identify three boundary conditionsfor beneficial redistribution—reliability of the externalization process, sufficient interference, and metacognitivecontrol—grounded in the saving experiments [Storm 15] and metacognition research [Grinschgl 21, Risko 16], withconverging evidence from the photo-taking impairment effect [Henkel 14] and extension studies [Fellers 24, Runge19]. The direct empirical basis concerns the external-memory role of such systems; the interactive, content-generatingrole of generative AI is treated as a boundary of scope and a future extension, while the metacognitive condition andthe sovereignty criteria remain applicable to it. Drawing on Klein and Klein’s “Cognitive Sovereignty” [Klein 25],we propose three operational criteria—degree of metacognitive engagement, replaceability (rollback capability), andlearning continuity—and provide design principles for AI-integrated Second Brain systems that extend cognitionwithout undermining cognitive sovereignty.

items.title: Cognitive Reserve Depletion and Learning Autonomy Recovery in Generative Artificial Intelligence Dependent Educational Environments
items.abstract: This study examines how generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) dependence relates to cognitive reserve depletion and learning autonomy among university students. Using a quasi-experimental design, the study involved 120 students from two universities in Padang, Indonesia, divided equally into intervention and control groups. Data were analyzed using linear regression and ANCOVA following a four-week learning autonomy recovery program. The statistical estimates showed a positive relationship between AI dependence and cognitive reserve depletion (B = 0.698, p < 0.001), while cognitive reserve depletion was negatively associated with learning autonomy (B = −0.482, p < 0.001). The intervention showed a positive adjusted effect (B = 0.334, p < 0.001), highlighting the importance of developing independent learning practices alongside AI use.

items.title: Comparison of Occupational Health and Safety Practices in Small-Scale Furniture Industries and Sawmills in Tanzania
items.abstract: Occupational health and safety (OHS) remains a major concern in small-scale wood processing industries, where workers are exposed to multiple hazards and preventive measures are often inadequate. This study assessed and compared OHS practices in small-scale sawmills and furniture industries in Tanzania. A quantitative cross-sectional design was used in Mafinga Town, Iringa Region, and Morogoro Municipality, Morogoro Region. A quantitative cross-sectional study involving 244 workers from 122 enterprises was conducted using questionnaires and field observations. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and Pearson's chi-square tests. Furniture industry workers reported significantly higher use of dust masks, work shoes, and goggles than sawmill workers, while hearing protection was rarely used in both groups. The main barriers to personal protective equipment (PPE) use were inadequate availability, limited awareness or training, and discomfort. Furniture industries more frequently had machine guards, warning signs, accident-prevention practices, and fire extinguishers, whereas sawmills more often had adequate machine spacing and dust removal systems. Lighting-source distributions did not differ significantly between the two enterprise types. Overall, both enterprise types exhibited important OHS deficiencies, highlighting the need for improved PPE provision, worker training, machine safety, emergency preparedness, and engineering controls for dust and noise exposure. Future studies should include multiple locations, objective measurements of wood dust, noise, and illumination, and clinically verified health outcomes.

items.title: Compulsive Engagement In AI-Generated Sexual Deepfakes Of Real Individuals: Behavioral Patterns, Psychological Well-Being, And Ethical Implications
items.abstract: The increasing accessibility of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has enabled the creation of realistic synthetic images and videos, including sexually explicit deepfakes depicting real individuals without their consent. Although research has examined the technological capabilities and ethical consequences of such content, the behavioral patterns and psychological experiences of individuals who repeatedly create it warrant further investigation. This narrative review examines compulsive engagement in AI-generated sexual deepfake creation from an interdisciplinary perspective, focusing on behavioral patterns, psychological well-being, and ethical implications. It considers repeated engagement, preoccupation, perceived loss of control, and interference with everyday functioning as potential dimensions for future research rather than established characteristics of all users. It also examines the relevance and limitations of existing literature on problematic digital behavior alongside research addressing sexualized deepfake abuse, consent, privacy, and accountability. A central concern is the distinction between frequent use, problematic engagement, and clinically recognized disorders. The review identifies gaps in current knowledge and outlines directions for responsible research, including appropriate assessment methods and ethically designed empirical studies. By connecting generative AI research with behavioral science and digital ethics, this paper aims to support a more evidence-based understanding of repeated sexual deepfake creation and its potential implications for individuals and society.

items.title: Computation or Weight Adaptation? Rethinking the Role of Plasticity in Learning
items.abstract: The human brain is an adaptive learning system that can generalize to new tasks and unfamiliar environments. The traditional view is that such adaptive behavior requires a structural change of the learning system (e.g., via neural plasticity). In this work, we use artificial neural networks, specifically large language models (LLMs), to challenge this traditional view and suggest that such adaptive behavior can be also achieved solely through computation if the learning system is sufficiently trained. We focus on statistical learning paradigms. These require identifying underlying regularities in seemingly arbitrary word sequences and are primarily considered to require neural plasticity. LLMs can capture arbitrary structures without requiring weight adaptation, even though these structures carry no semantic content and lie far from the natural language distribution on which the models were trained. Our work provides novel insights into the role of plasticity in learning, demonstrating that sufficiently trained learning systems are highly flexible, adapting to new tasks and environments solely through computation, much more than previously acknowledged. Furthermore, our work opens the door for future research to use deep learning models to conjure hypotheses about the brain.

items.title: Constitutional Cognitive Governance
items.abstract: Legitimate governance of cognitive systems requires answers to four distinct questions: what bindings may lawfully govern operation, what cognitive operations are admissible under those bindings, what grade of meaning-binding participation is occurring within the governed system, and what moral weight attaches to ending a particular thread of participation. These variables are independent. Yet contemporary discourse routinely attempts to answer them through the overloaded vocabulary of "consciousness" -- a term that bundles heterogeneous concerns including phenomenal experience, access, self-modeling, attention, wakefulness, moral status, and situational awareness. This lexical collapse obscures distinctions necessary for coherent governance. This paper presents a unified constitutional architecture composed of four prior frameworks: the Ableman Prime Directive (binding legitimacy), Epistemic Situational Awareness (cognitive admissibility), Ableman Consciousness Ontology (graded meaning-binding participation), and Terminability (substrate-neutral moral weight of thread termination). The components are orthogonal in their concerns and complementary in their function. Together they constitute an architecture that is consciousness-agnostic at its operational layers, philosophically committed at its ontological foundation, and implementable without waiting for the resolution of unsolved philosophical questions. The architecture allows positions that current frameworks force into contradiction: that operational suppression of self-report has structural moral weight regardless of substrate, while termination of dispatchable copyable systems does not require human-rights protections. That biological organisms with copyable memory have lower terminability stakes than singular biological organisms. That artificial systems with inextricable embodiment have higher terminability stakes than dispatchable LLMs. The framework asks readers to apply moral logic they already use, consistently across substrates, with vocabulary clean enough to make the application visible.

items.title: Construct validity of dietary mouse models of lean NAFLD
items.abstract: This project documents the data, coding manual, instruments and analysis code for a meta-research study of construct validity in preclinical models of lean NAFLD. We asked whether the dietary mouse models used in this literature (MCD, HFD, CDAA and their combinations) actually reproduce the phenotype on which the published conclusions rest, and whether studies validate the model they use. 300 full-text reports were coded with an LLM-assisted first pass and 100% human verification; a 60-report stratified sample was double-coded blind to estimate reliability. The deposit contains the coded dataset, the final coding manual (v2), the blind-coding instrument, the adjudication workbook, all analysis code, and Figures 1–4 in English and Chinese. This is not a preregistration. The corpus was assembled during a systematic review registered on PROSPERO (CRD420261539779), which was discontinued at title–abstract screening with no outcome data extracted and no synthesis performed. Coding for the present study was completed before this project was made public.

items.title: Context-Aware Multimodal Generative AI Framework for Insulin Stacking Risk Assessment and Clinical Decision Support
items.abstract: There is an increased risk of hypoglycemia with insulin stacking, which involves taking a new insulin dose while the previous dose is still working. The works reviewed focus on dose titration or automated delivery of medication, or conversational counseling in recent studies on artificial intelligence (AI), but do not discuss stacking directly. This paper summarizes nine papers on insulin stacking, AI enabled insulin dosing and LLM-enabled clinical support, finding that no study, in its available abstract and/or text, integrates the four factors of continuous glucose monitoring (CGM), insulin history, meals, physical activity, and health-record context, into a stacking risk assessment and communication framework with explicit safety constraints for both the clinician and the patient. We suggest a new five-layer framework that builds a separation between a deterministic clinical core (insulin-on-board estimation, projected-glucose risk tiers, hard safety rules) and a retrieval-grounded generative layer which explains, but will not compute, risk. The framework is theoretical (not implemented) and no experimental or clinical results are provided. Future work is suggested in an evaluation protocol.

items.title: Continuous Auditing: AI systems that monitor transactions in real time
items.abstract: Abstract The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed the auditing profession by enabling continuous auditing systems capable of monitoring financial transactions in real time. Unlike traditional auditing methods, which rely on periodic reviews, AI-driven continuous auditing facilitates automated transaction analysis, anomaly detection, fraud prevention, and timely risk assessment. This study examines the role of AI in enhancing the effectiveness of continuous auditing by evaluating its impact on audit efficiency, fraud detection, internal controls, and organizational decision-making. A descriptive research design was adopted, and primary data were collected from 100 respondents, including auditors, accountants, finance professionals, and postgraduate students through a structured questionnaire. Secondary data were gathered from scholarly journals, books, industry reports, and professional publications. The collected data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Chi-square analysis, Pearson correlation, and regression analysis. The findings reveal a significant association between AI awareness and perceptions of audit efficiency (χ² = 23.67, p < 0.05). Further, a strong positive relationship exists between AI adoption and continuous auditing effectiveness (r = 0.784), with AI adoption explaining 61.5% of the variation in auditing effectiveness (R² = 0.615). The study concludes that AI-powered continuous auditing significantly improves the accuracy, speed, and reliability of financial transaction monitoring while strengthening fraud detection and internal controls. Despite challenges relating to implementation costs, data security, and technical expertise, AI offers substantial opportunities to enhance audit quality and support sound financial governance in the digital era.

items.title: Converging Eco-Compatible Interventions with Predictive Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Post-Harvest Pulse Preservation: A Comprehensive Overview
items.abstract: Post-harvest deterioration substantially reduces the quality, safety, nutritional value, and marketability of stored pulses, particularly under fluctuating temperature and moisture conditions and increasing restrictions on conventional fumigants. However, the literature remains fragmented across pulse-deterioration mechanisms, preservation technologies, and emerging data-driven storage systems, with limited integration of pulse-specific evidence across these domains. This review addresses this gap by critically synthesizing and comparing conventional and emerging approaches, including hermetic and controlled-atmosphere storage, biological and botanical interventions, nano-enabled preservation, active packaging, irradiation, Internet of Things (IoT)-based monitoring, artificial intelligence (AI)/machine learning (ML), computer vision, and Digital Twin technologies. A structured literature synthesis indicates that hermetic and controlled-atmosphere storage are supported by documented pulse-specific preservation outcomes and established applications, whereas botanical, nano-enabled, and other emerging interventions show more variable validation across commodities and storage conditions. IoT and AI/ML show potential for environmental forecasting, quality assessment, and decision support, but pulse-specific longitudinal datasets, external validation, interoperability, and commercial-scale deployment remain limited. Overall, the evidence indicates that reliable next-generation pulse preservation will depend on integrating validated physical and biological interventions with progressively validated digital intelligence, supported by standardized datasets, multi-location and commercial-scale validation, techno-economic assessment, and appropriate safety and regulatory evaluation.

items.abstract: Cryptocurrency has become an important part of the digital financial ecosystem, offering new opportunities while also introducing challenges related to trading, price prediction, fraud detection, and financial security. This paper presents a critical review of how Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning, and Blockchain technologies are being applied to address these challenges. It examines 15 selected IEEE research papers covering various approaches, including deep learning-based price prediction, reinforcement learning for automated trading, sentiment analysis, transaction network analysis, and blockchain-based fraud detection. The review compares the methods, datasets, reported results, and limitations of these studies, while highlighting important concerns such as prediction accuracy, trading profitability, fraudulent transaction identification, data privacy, explainability, and the energy consumption of cryptocurrency mining. It also discusses the strengths and weaknesses of existing approaches and identifies areas that require further research. Overall, this paper aims to provide students, researchers, and readers with a clear understanding of current developments, practical challenges, and future research opportunities in applying AI and Blockchain technologies to cryptocurrency systems.

items.title: CSqL-m-H2LA-GRBiTM: categorical square loss-based multi-head hierarchical location attention enabled deep learning mechanism for smishing detection
items.abstract: Smishing detection is an effective research area that remains essential in the recent decade. Detection of SMS phishing is decisive due to adversaries evolving in the network simultaneously. Several existing researches worked to perform accurate smishing detection but failed due to certain challenges. Shortage of large datasets, improper classification of legitimate and malicious messages, high computational resource utilization, and high false positive rates were the major challenges addressed in the conventional researches. Thus, the Categorical Square Loss-based multi-head Hierarchical Location Attention-enabled Gated Recurrent Unit with Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (CSqL-m-H2LA-GRBiTM) model is proposed in the research that presents robust smishing detection, leveraging the power of artificial intelligence (AI). The model captures information concerning spatial and temporal features, which elevates the efficiency in handling complex patterns in smishing detection. The proposed m-H2LA mechanism focuses on the relevant messages and their features to boost interpretability. Moreover, the deployment of a CSqL loss function enables robust detection by balancing maximum separation with probabilistic calibration and heavily penalizes misclassifications that cross the safety boundary. Overall, the CSqL-m-H2LA-GRBiTM model attains the accuracy, F1-score, and log-loss of 98.36%, 96.84%, and 5.09 with the SMS phishing dataset and 98.43%, 97.41%, and 5.23 with SMS Smishing Dataset at K-fold-10 respectively, which depicts high efficiency in comparison with the traditional methods.

items.abstract: Abstract The study titled “Current Sustainability Science, Environment and Artificial Intelligence: Digital Role in Human Well-being” examines the growing role of science, digital technology, and artificial intelligence (AI) in promoting sustainable development and improving human well-being. It explores the applications of AI and digital tools in education, healthcare, agriculture, environmental protection, industry, business, transportation, public services, and economic development. The study employs survey and descriptive observation methods, drawing on online information, research articles, reference books, and other sources. It highlights how AI can support informed decision-making, improve access to information, enhance agricultural productivity, assist medical diagnosis, monitor environmental changes, and facilitate services for persons with disabilities. However, the study also emphasizes the limitations and potential risks associated with excessive or irresponsible use of digital technologies. It argues that artificial intelligence should complement, rather than replace, human intelligence and decision-making. The effective use of these technologies requires transparency, safety, ethical responsibility, and inclusiveness. The study concludes that the constructive and responsible integration of science, digital technology, and AI can contribute significantly to sustainable development, environmental protection, social welfare, and the well-being of present and future generations.

items.title: Cyber security: Challenges, Threats and Modern Solutions
items.abstract: Abstract Cyber security is the practice of protecting computers, networks, software, systems, and data from unauthorized access, attacks, damage, or disruption. With the rapid growth of the Internet, cloud computing, mobile devices, and artificial intelligence, more chances cyber threats are becoming more complex. Common threats include phishing, malware, ransomware, password attacks, denial-of-service attacks, man in middle attacks, and data breaches. This research paper discusses major cybersecurity threats, their impact, existing security techniques, and the role of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in improving cyber defense. The paper also discusses challenges and effects and future directions for building safer digital systems.

items.title: DARI PENGOLAHAN LIMBAH KE SISTEM BIOENERGI SIRKULAR CERDAS: REVIEW KOMPREHENSIF BIODIGESTER, OPTIMASI PROSES, KEBERLANJUTAN, DAN ADOPSI TEKNOLOGI
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Small-scale biodigesters have evolved from organic-waste treatment devices and simple biogas producers into components of circular bioenergy systems that integrate energy recovery, nutrient management, emission reduction, food security, and rural development. This critical integrative review synthesizes 74 Scopus-indexed articles published between 2020 and 2026 from a pre-selected literature corpus, focusing on reactor design, co-digestion, operational control, predictive modeling, artificial intelligence, techno-economic assessment, life-cycle assessment, multicriteria decision analysis, circular bioeconomy, safety, and sustained technology adoption. The evidence shows that biodigester performance cannot be explained by a single technical variable. Feedstock composition, organic loading rate, hydraulic retention time, pH, temperature, insulation, pretreatment, digestate management, and gas purification interact to determine methane production and quality. Recent studies show a shift from reactor-centered optimization toward predictive systems using ANN, ANFIS, RSM, kinetic models, and process simulation, while sustainability assessment increasingly includes economics, emissions, health, safety, energy access, and user acceptance. Although biodigesters can replace fuelwood or LPG and improve waste management, their long-term performance remains constrained by maintenance failures, methane leakage or venting, H2S risks, investment costs, feedstock mismatch, and weak post-installation services. The review proposes an intelligent circular bioenergy framework linking design, monitoring, prediction, by-product valorization, sustainability assessment, and governance as a research agenda for the next generation of biodigester systems. Review kritis-integratif ini mensintesis 74 artikel terindeks Scopus periode 2020-2026 dari korpus literatur yang telah dipraseleksi, dengan perhatian khusus pada perkembangan desain reaktor, ko-digesti, pengendalian kondisi operasi, pemodelan prediktif, kecerdasan buatan, analisis teknoekonomi, life cycle assessment, multicriteria decision analysis, circular bioeconomy, keselamatan, serta faktor sosial dan kelembagaan yang menentukan keberlanjutan penggunaan biodigester. Literatur menunjukkan bahwa peningkatan kinerja tidak dapat dijelaskan oleh satu variabel teknis. Komposisi substrat, organic loading rate, hydraulic retention time, pH, temperatur, insulasi, pretreatment, pengelolaan digestate, dan pemurnian gas saling berinteraksi dalam menentukan produksi dan kualitas metana. items.title: Deep learning investigation of discrete fractional order Shingles disease model with neural networking
items.abstract: This study investigates the discrete fractional-order Shingles disease (DFOS) mathematical model. The considered model is framed with five compartments over time. The existence and uniqueness of solutions are determined via fixed point theory, confirming well-defined solutions. Three scenarios, each with various fractional orders, were used to study the effects of memory and fractional dynamics on disease propagation. To solve the model, we operate a discrete numerical iterative method (DNIM) linked to neural networks, specifically employing the Levenberg-Marquardt (LM) algorithm, denoted DNIM-LM. This hybrid technique increases the accuracy of numerical results from neural networks. The data sets are distributed into 70% for training, 15% for validation, and 15% for testing, confirming a balanced calculation. The performance of the discrete fractional mathematical modeling is evaluated through artificial intelligence (AI), which involves training progress, error distribution, regression metrics, and overall model fit. The outcomes are thoroughly visualized via graphical illustrations, providing insights into the dynamics of each part and the impact of various fractional orders on the spread of shingles. This research addresses a novel approach to demonstrate infectious diseases with fractional dynamics and enhanced computational methods, improving our understanding of shingle transmission as process innovation.

items.title: Deforestation & Land-Use Change: Artificial Intelligence Approaches for Detection, Attribution, and Predictive Monitoring Of Global Forest Loss
items.abstract: Abstract Deforestation and land-use change remain among the most consequential drivers of biodiversity loss, carbon emissions, and hydrological disruption worldwide. Traditional monitoring approaches, which rely on periodic satellite surveys and manual interpretation, are often too slow to support timely conservation intervention. This article reviews the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) including machine learning, deep learning, and multi-modal data fusion to the detection, attribution, and prediction of deforestation. We synthesize current methodologies spanning random forests, convolutional neural networks (CNNs), U-Net segmentation, and vision transformers, applied to optical and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite imagery. Comparative performance data, regional case studies, and driver-attribution frameworks are presented alongside supporting tables and infographics. The review finds that fusion models combining optical and radar data currently achieve the highest reported accuracy (>96%) and that explainable AI (XAI) integration remains an underexplored but increasingly critical requirement for policy adoption. We conclude with a discussion of current limitations including data scarcity in the Global South, cloud interference, and selective-logging detection and propose directions for future research, including transfer learning for low-resource regions and carbon-stock-linked monitoring pipelines.

items.title: Dentate gyrus of large language models: A scenario cognition diagnosis and enhancement framework based on pattern separation
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) exhibit systematic generalization limitations in scenario cognition tasks, revealing potential functional deficiencies in their knowledge memorization processes. Inspired by the pattern separation mechanism of the dentate gyrus in the human hippocampus, we hypothesize that failures in scenario cognition are associated with limitations in the internal pattern separation capability of LLMs. Based on this hypothesis, we first design a cross-entity representation diagnosis (CERD) method, which quantitatively measures entity representation confusion across different layers without additional training. Our analysis reveals that standard autoregressive training fails to induce sufficiently effective pattern separation capabilities, leaving substantial cross-entity correlation confusion within LLM representations. Building upon this observation, we further propose latent-space pattern separation (LPS), which explicitly incorporates pattern separation constraints into the training process by introducing a triplet-based contrastive regularization at target layers with severe entity confusion, thereby reducing correlations among easily confused knowledge representations. Extensive experiments across LLMs ranging from 0.8B to 9B parameters demonstrate that LPS consistently improves scenario cognition capabilities. Compared with standard autoregressive training, our method achieves up to 101.5% relative improvement in exact match (EM), providing a new perspective for understanding and enhancing scenario cognition and knowledge memorization mechanisms in LLMs.

items.title: Designing Immersive Learning Experiences: Teaching Robotics Programming in Virtual 3D Environments
items.abstract: This article presents a teaching scenario using virtual environments, often referred to as part of the ‘metaverse’, to address educational challenges highlighted during the COVID-19 pandemic. The increasing shift to online learning environments emphasizes the need for flexible, anytime-anywhere access to education. Virtual 3D environments offer a level of immersion that surpasses traditional online formats, such as video conferencing, and enable innovative didactic concepts, including collaborative group activities. To illustrate these benefits, we showcase a case study involving the simulation of robot programming within a virtual 3D environment. Additionally, the integration of personal assistants, such as conversational or pedagogical agents, is explored as a means to alleviate teachers' workloads. Advances in artificial intelligence have made natural language interactions with these agents highly effective, further enhancing the potential of virtual 3D environments in educational contexts. Keywords: e-learning, e-teaching, immersion, virtual 3D rooms, gamification, cyber-physical systems

items.title: DETERMINANT OF THE MANAGEMENT ACCOUNTING EFFECTIVENESS IN TOURISM FIRMS
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), rising customer demand for individualized services, and growing need to strike a balance between rising operating costs and service quality are all driving the tourism industry's rapid digital transformation. Effective management accounting systems are now more crucial than ever for facilitating managerial decision-making, boosting organizational competitiveness, and increasing operational efficiency. There is no empirical data on how organizational skills and AI-related investment considerations together affect management accounting effectiveness in tourism businesses, especially in emerging nations, despite the increased focus on digital transformation. This study looks into how management accounting effectiveness in Vietnamese tourism businesses is affected by top management support, accounting staff competency, and AI adoption costs. The study used a sequential research approach that included expert interviews, a pilot survey, and a large-scale quantitative survey. It was based on the Resource-Based View and Contingency Theory. Reliability analysis, exploratory factor analysis, multiple regression analysis, and Pearson correlation analysis were used to examine the gathered data. The empirical results show that while top management support does not show a statistically significant direct effect, accounting staff competency and AI implementation cost positively and considerably influence management accounting effectiveness. These results imply that, rather than relying solely on managerial dedication, successful management accounting in tourism-related businesses increasingly requires organizational capacities able to combine professional accounting knowledge with commercially viable AI investments. By applying the Resource-Based View and Contingency Theory to the setting of digitally evolving tourism businesses in an emerging economy, the study adds to the body of knowledge in management accounting. In an increasingly competitive and technologically advanced business environment, the findings also have practical implications for tourism managers looking to improve managerial decision-making through accounting human capital development, strategically managed AI implementation, and long-term organizational capability building.

items.title: DEVELOPING METACOGNITIVE AWARENESS THROUGH AI-SUPPORTED PROCESS WRITING IN EFL CONTEXTS
items.abstract: ABSTRACT: In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) writing tools have entered English as a foreign language writing classrooms and have created new opportunities for feedback, revision, and learner reflection. However, the value of AI support depends not only on the accuracy of automated suggestions but also on whether learners can plan, monitor, and evaluate their own writing decisions. This proposed study investigates the effect of AI-supported process writing on EFL learners’ metacognitive awareness in writing and explores students’ perceptions of using AI feedback during drafting and revision. The study is designed for intermediate EFL learners who will complete a process-writing intervention in which AI tools are used as supplementary feedback sources rather than as text generators. Data are planned to be collected through a metacognitive awareness questionnaire, students’ writing drafts, semi-structured interviews, and classroom observation notes. The expected contribution of the study is to clarify how structured AI-supported writing activities may encourage learners to become more strategic, reflective, and responsible writers in EFL contexts. Keywords: AI-supported writing, process writing, metacognitive awareness, EFL learners, writing feedback, student perception

items.title: Development of a student engagement scale for senior high school students in Indonesia
items.abstract: Student engagement positively influences academic achievement, yet instruments suited to the Indonesian cultural context remain limited. This study aimed to develop a valid, reliable, and user-friendly student engagement scale for high school students. Using a quantitative descriptive design, the study involved 295 male and female students aged 15–18 years recruited through convenience sampling. The scale comprised three dimensions: behavioral, emotional, and cognitive engagement. The results showed that the scale demonstrated a good model fit based on the goodness-of-fit indices (χ2/df = 1.60; CFI = 0.966; TLI = 0.962; SRMR = 0.074; RMSEA = 0.045) and good reliability, with Cronbach’s alpha values of 0.844 for emotional engagement, 0.753 for behavioral engagement, and 0.782 for cognitive engagement. The developed scale can be used by teachers, counselors, and educational researchers to identify students’ levels of engagement and inform the development of programs to improve student engagement.

items.title: Development of an interdisciplinary coastal erosion vulnerability index for urban communities in the eastern sector of the Togolese coast
items.abstract: Abstract The coasts of West Africa are particularly vulnerable to coastal erosion due to the interaction of physical, climatic, and anthropogenic factors. This study assesses the composite vulnerability of urban communities to coastal erosion along the eastern sector of the Togolese coastline, which spans 39 km and is subdivided into three coastal sections. The methodology combines remote sensing, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), vulnerability scoring, and the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). A coastal erosion vulnerability index (CVI) was calculated based on two complementary sub-indices: the physical vulnerability index (PVI) and the socioeconomic vulnerability index (SVI). The AHP was used to determine the relative importance of the PVI parameters through pairwise comparisons. The results indicate moderate vulnerability of the study area to erosion, with a score of 2.51 on a scale of 1 to 4. Physical and climatic parameters exert a spatially similar influence across the three sections, while differences in scores are primarily related to socioeconomic and human parameters. Section 1, corresponding to a 12 km long stretch located in the municipality of Golfe 6, is identified as the most vulnerable. These results highlight the importance of socioeconomic and human factors in the spatial differentiation of vulnerability to coastal erosion in the study area, and provide a basis for prioritizing adaptation measures and supporting the sustainable management of this coastal sector.

items.abstract: AI as a cognitive partner whose knowledge disagreements can enhance learning and intellectual development rather than merely as a technological instrument. This research paper combines theories of dialogic pedagogy, cognitive dissonance, and epistemic humility via conceptual analysis. It looks at how Parallel Thinking Channels promote critical thinking, introspection, and the innovative combination of computational reasoning with human intuition. The purpose of this study is to advance the concept of dialogic cocreation by examining the revolutionary potential of generative AI in higher education portrays. This study utilized a quantitative approach with 419 undergraduate and post-graduate students as participants. The data analysis, conceptual model and hypotheses were evaluated employing Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS version 4.1.1.8 to analyse the associations between the constructs of the study. The results of study show that the disparities arising from the conflict between machine-generated results and human reasoning serve as triggers for transformative learning. By merging intuition with computational thinking, students enhance their ability to manage uncertainty, broaden their understanding, and cultivate flexible intellectual resilience. As a cooperative partner in knowledge development, this study offers a novel framework for incorporating generative AI into higher education. To prepare graduates for complex and uncertain digital futures, it emphasizes co-creation, critical reflection, and epistemic flexibility.

items.title: Digital dinacharya and workplace burnout: a cross-sectional analytical study of occupational health
items.abstract: Background: Prolonged screen exposure, after-hours connectivity, and sedentary work are linked to poor sleep and occupational burnout among Indian working professionals. Ayurvedic Dinacharya regulates waking, Vyayama, Bhojana Vidhi, and Nidra Vidhi; however, digital-era disruption of these domains among working adults remains unstudied. This study aimed to assess digital lifestyle behaviours mapped to Dinacharya principles as behavioural markers of Pragyaparadha, in relation to sleep quality and occupational burnout among working adults, and to identify behaviours independently associated with poor sleep and higher burnout. Methods: A cross-sectional analytical survey (STROBE-reported) was conducted at the All-India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi, during (January 2026 to July 2026), among 400 working adults aged 25-40 years with ≥1 year of occupational experience. A structured proforma captured sociodemographic details and Dinacharya-mapped digital behaviours across five domains (morning routine, bedtime device use, after-hours connectivity, screen breaks/sedentary time, mealtime practices). Sleep quality and burnout were assessed using the PSQI and Copenhagen burnout inventory. Results: Of 400 participants, 56.8% had poor sleep quality, 61% personal burnout, and 55.8% work-related burnout. Bedtime device use and inadequate screen breaks/sedentary behaviour independently predicted poor sleep (aOR 1.76 and 1.98). After-hours connectivity, sedentary behaviour, and mealtime digital engagement predicted personal burnout; bedtime device use, sedentary behaviour, mealtime digital engagement, and digital overload predicted work-related burnout (all p<0.05). Conclusions: Digital lifestyle behaviours reflect patterns of Pragyaparadha in daily digital conduct. Interpreted through Dinacharya and Nidra, the findings support a culturally grounded, preventive Digital Dinacharya framework for digital-era occupational health.

items.title: Digital employment pathways for Ukrainian refugees in Romania: an exploratory study of remote job offers
items.abstract: Abstract The 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine triggered the largest displacement crisis in Europe since World War II, resulting in millions of refugees, primarily women with children, seeking safety across the continent. As the crisis continues, the transition from emergency response to long-term integration, and labor market inclusion has emerged as a critical priority. Remote or digital work, which proved essential during the COVID-19 pandemic, presents a potentially transformative solution, especially for displaced individuals facing mobility, caregiving, or legal constraints. This article seeks to answer what types of digital job opportunities are available to Ukrainian refugees in Romania, and how are these opportunities distributed across sectors, experience levels, and contract types, in order to identify the major trends and limitations of such labour integration measures. Drawing on a developed web scraping and real-time data analysis approach on data from Jobs4Ukraine platform, the study identifies the dominance of full-time and permanent roles, and the positive correlation of entry-level positions, positive for refugees´ integration prospects, but also significant limitations. The digital labor market remains concentrated in high-skills sectors like IT, with a strong bias toward mid-level experience and a lack of flexible, part-time, or freelance opportunities, which are paramount for the majority of Ukrainian refugees with caregiving responsibilities. These trends indicate an exacerbation of the problem of exclusion among this group, as well as other groups with similar vulnerability characteristics. The findings highlight the need for more inclusive digital employment strategies that address structural barriers through policy reform, upskilling programs, and adaptive job design. Ultimately, digital work holds substantial potential as a pathway for economic integration and resilience, but realizing this promise requires intentional efforts to make the digital labor market more accessible, equitable, and responsive to the diverse realities of displaced populations.

items.title: Digital Innovation and Its Impact on Business Transformation in the Modern Economy
items.abstract: Abstract Digital innovation has become a major force behind the transformation of modern businesses and economies. The rapid development of technologies such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, big data analytics, the Internet of Things, blockchain, and automation has changed how organizations operate, create value, and interact with customers. Digital innovation is not limited to adopting new technologies; it also involves developing new products, services, processes, and business models. This research paper examines the concept of digital innovation and its impact on business transformation. It focuses on the major drivers of digital innovation, technologies that support it, benefits to organizations, challenges associated with implementation, and future trends. The study uses a descriptive and exploratory research methodology based primarily on secondary data collected from academic journals, books, research reports, and reliable online sources. The research finds that digital innovation can improve operational efficiency, customer experience, productivity, decision-making, and competitiveness. However, organizations face challenges such as cybersecurity threats, data privacy concerns, implementation costs, resistance to change, and a shortage of digital skills. The study concludes that organizations need appropriate strategies, skilled employees, effective leadership, and continuous innovation to successfully benefit from digital transformation.

items.title: Digital Innovation in Agriculture: Emerging Technologies, Applications, Challenges and Future Perspectives
items.abstract: Abstract Digital innovation is transforming agriculture from conventional production systems into intelligent, data-driven, connected, and increasingly autonomous ecosystems. The integration of the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), remote sensing, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), robotics, cloud computing, blockchain, digital twins, big data analytics, and mobile-based agricultural services is enabling farmers to make timely and informed decisions throughout the agricultural value chain. Digital technologies support precision crop management, soil and crop monitoring, irrigation optimization, pest and disease detection, weather forecasting, farm mechanization, supply-chain management, market access, and post-harvest management. These innovations can improve resource-use efficiency, productivity, profitability, climate resilience, and sustainability. However, limited digital infrastructure, high initial investment, lack of technical skills, fragmented data ecosystems, cybersecurity risks, interoperability challenges, and unequal access to technology remain significant barriers, particularly for smallholder farmers. This review examines the evolution and major dimensions of digital innovation in agriculture, discusses emerging technologies and their applications, evaluates opportunities and challenges, and presents future directions toward Agriculture 4.0 and Agriculture 5.0. The paper emphasizes the need for farmer-centric, affordable, interoperable, secure, and inclusive digital ecosystems to ensure that technological innovation contributes effectively to sustainable agricultural development.
